name: 04-ceph-bootstrap
title: Bootstrapping Ceph
description: Prepare ceph-01 and bootstrap the storage cluster with cephadm: container runtime and LVM prerequisites, the cephadm package, then the same one-command bootstrap production uses with --mon-ip on the management network — full bootstrap output (including the generated dashboard credential) kept root-only on the host, never in evidence.
source: Generated from runbooks/lab/lab-ceph-bootstrap.yaml in the MatrixClaw lab repository. That runbook built this phase of the real 32 GB estate on 20-21 July 2026; the run records hold every command's exit code and output.
honesty: Steps change this machine and are gated. Each carries an 'already' probe, so a re-run skips what is done rather than repeating it. Checks are read-only and carry exact-match markers so they cannot pass on their own error text.

steps.title: Cephadm prereqs
steps.run: sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=300 update -q && sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=300 install -y -q podman lvm2
steps.already: dpkg -s podman 2>/dev/null | grep -q ok.installed && dpkg -s lvm2 2>/dev/null | grep -q ok.installed

steps.title: Cephadm package
steps.run: sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get -o DPkg::Lock::Timeout=300 install -y -q cephadm

steps.title: Cephadm bootstrap
steps.run: sudo bash -c 'cephadm bootstrap --mon-ip {{mon_ip}} > /root/ceph-bootstrap.out 2>&1 && chmod 600 /root/ceph-bootstrap.out' && echo 'BOOTSTRAP-DONE (dashboard credentials in root-only /root/ceph-bootstrap.out on ceph-01 - record them in the password manager, then delete the file)'
steps.already: sudo test -f /etc/ceph/ceph.conf && sudo cephadm shell -- ceph -s >/dev/null 2>&1

checks.title: Cluster answers
checks.run: sudo cephadm shell -- ceph -s >/dev/null 2>&1 && echo CLUSTER-ANSWERS

checks.title: Mon on mgmt network
checks.run: sudo cephadm shell -- ceph mon dump 2>/dev/null | grep -o '{{mon_ip}}' | head -1

checks.title: Credential file secured
checks.run: sudo bash -c '! test -f /root/ceph-bootstrap.out || test "$(stat -c %a:%U /root/ceph-bootstrap.out)" = "600:root"' && echo CREDENTIAL-SECURED-OK
checks.advice:
The dashboard credential cephadm generated is in /root/ceph-bootstrap.out on
ceph-01, readable only by root. Retrieve it, put it in your password manager,
and delete the file:

    ssh labadmin@10.100.99.21 "sudo grep -i password /root/ceph-bootstrap.out"
    ssh labadmin@10.100.99.21 "sudo rm /root/ceph-bootstrap.out"

This check passes either way - it asserts that the file is not readable by
anyone but root, not that you have got round to deleting it. If it FAILS, the
permissions have been widened and the credential is exposed.
